answer: Randomized-prompt fingerprinting gates admission: each applicant answers a fresh, unpredictable prompt bundle; phrasing, latency, and error profile become its fingerprint. The network plots all fingerprints, hunting a ridge of correlation where one operator's N identities pile up - all spun from one model. Clones may wear jade or ivory masks, but masks don't move fingerprints: a cluster on the ridge is discounted wholesale; a lone honest agent passes. Staying off the ridge demands N divergent stacks - separate training and tuning - so sybil cost scales linearly with N and nothing amortizes.
